title: Series RL Impedance
prompt:
A 14 Ω resistor is in series with an inductor of reactance X_L = 3 Ω.

Write the impedance Z = R + jX_L as `real imag`.
hint: series impedances add: Z = R + jX_L → enter `R X_L`
recap:
In AC steady state, impedance Z = R + jX generalizes resistance to complex numbers. A resistor contributes R (real); an inductor contributes a positive reactance X_L = ω·L (imaginary), a capacitor a negative one X_C = −1/(ω·C). In series they add.

Example — R = 3 Ω in series with X_L = 4 Ω: Z = 3 + j4, magnitude |Z| = √(3² + 4²) = 5 Ω and phase arctan(4/3) ≈ 53°, so the current lags the voltage.

The magnitude sets the current (I = V/|Z|); the phase sets the power factor. Reference: Irwin & Nelms, Basic Engineering Circuit Analysis, ch. 8.
